## Package overview

`selectFiberseqLociWorkflow` visualizes m6A methylation and per-read footprints
at selected genomic loci using processed tracks from fibertools and FiberHMM.
You choose the samples, methylation and footprint files, genomic coordinates,
and footprint length filters. The package produces m6A heatmaps, aggregate
m6A profiles and footprint panels, with optional clustering of reads by their
m6A patterns.

The required m6A input is fibertools BED12. Optional tracks include fibertools
or FiberHMM nucleosomes, FiberHMM or custom per-read TF footprints, and FIRE
intervals. Human, plant and other genomes are supported when contig names and
reference assemblies agree across inputs. The package reads processed tracks;
it does not call methylation or footprints from raw sequencing data.

## Functions by task

Each function below links to a short tutorial on this page. Run the tutorials
in order for a complete analysis with the bundled LCL data. The reference
layout follows the concise function summaries in the
[trackViewer reference](https://jianhong.github.io/trackViewer/reference/index.html).

### Prepare sample inputs

| Function | What it does |
|:--|:--|
| [`example_data()`](#example-data) | Load a writable example dataset. |
| [`make_sample_sheet()`](#make-sample-sheet) | Define samples and track paths. |

| [`prepare_regions()`](#prepare-regions) | Define loci from coordinates or annotations. |
| [`extract_canonical_tss()`](#extract-canonical-tss) | Select canonical transcription start sites. |

| Function | What it does |
|:--|:--|
| [`validate_inputs()`](#validate-inputs) | Check files, indexes and contigs. |
| [`analyze_loci()`](#analyze-loci) | Collect locus data and optionally cluster reads. |

## Before you start

Install the package and its dependencies as described in the README, then load:

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
library(selectFiberseqLociWorkflow)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
```

Examples below execute with bundled files and temporary output directories.
Only the clearly marked own-data example needs paths supplied by you.

## Prepare sample inputs: tutorials

### `example_data()` — load test files {#example-data}

This function copies a small subset of real AL6 and AL8 LCL tracks around
ALAS1 and PRDX1 into a writable directory. It returns the sample sheet, region
ranges and copied directory. These files cover the example loci, not the
whole genome.

```{r example-data}
e <- example_data()
names(e)
e$samples[, c("sample_name", "sample_label")]
e$regions
```

The default destination is temporary. To keep the files, pass a new or empty
folder, for example `example_data("my-fiberseq-example")`.

### `make_sample_sheet()` — specify samples and files {#make-sample-sheet}

Create one row per sample. `sample_name` is a unique ID; `sample_label` is a
display or group label. The required columns are `sample_name`, `m6a` and
`m6a_format`. Optional tracks have their own path and format columns.

```{r make-sample-sheet}
sample_table <- as.data.frame(e$samples)
sample_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
samples <- make_sample_sheet(sample_table, output = sample_file)
samples[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a_format", "tf_format")]

# Reload the saved sample sheet in a later session.
samples <- make_sample_sheet(sample_file)
```

To select fewer samples, subset the rows of `sample_table` before calling
`make_sample_sheet()`. To use your own files, replace the paths in this example:

```{r own-samples, eval=FALSE}
sample_table <- data.frame(
    sample_name = c("sample_1", "sample_2"),
    sample_label = c("Control", "Treatment"),
    m6a = "/data/{sample_name}/m6a.{chr}.bed.gz",
    m6a_format = "bed12_fibertools",
    nucleosome = "/data/{sample_name}/nucleosome.{chr}.bed.gz",
    nucleosome_format = "bed13_fiberhmm",
    tf = "/data/{sample_name}/tf.{chr}.bed.gz",
    tf_format = "bed15_fiberhmm_tf"
)
samples <- make_sample_sheet(sample_table, output = "samples.tsv")
```

For `sample_1` on `Chr5`, the first template resolves to
`/data/sample_1/m6a.Chr5.bed.gz`. Only `{sample_name}` and `{chr}` are supported
placeholders. Whole-genome files can use explicit paths without `{chr}`.
Relative paths in a TSV are resolved against its directory; paths in an
in-memory table use `base_dir` (default: the working directory).

Each supplied track must be sorted, bgzip-compressed and accompanied by a
`.tbi` index. Omit optional columns or leave optional paths blank if no track
is available. The supported format strings are:

| Track | Format |
|:--|:--|
| m6A | `bed12_fibertools` |
| Nucleosome | `bed12_fibertools` or `bed13_fiberhmm` |
| TF footprint | `bed15_fiberhmm_tf` or `bed6_per_sample` |
| FIRE | `bed11_fire` |

Custom TF BED6 files use chromosome, zero-based start, end, original read ID,
score and strand. They must already be score-filtered. Footprint read IDs must
match the m6A read IDs within the same sample.

## Select genomic regions: tutorials

### `prepare_regions()` — choose loci {#prepare-regions}

Use coordinate strings for a quick custom interval. They are one-based and
inclusive. This example selects 1,000 bp within the bundled ALAS1 locus:

```{r prepare-regions}
regions <- prepare_regions("chr3:52197660-52198659")
names(regions) <- "ALAS1_custom"
regions
```

For several loci, supply several strings and give each a unique name. You can
also supply a coordinate table, a `GRanges`, a BED file, or a GTF/GFF3 annotation.
Contig names are preserved exactly, including case.

The following BED example describes the same interval. BED starts are
zero-based and ends are excluded; the region BED needs no tabix index.

```{r bed-regions}
bed_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed")
write.table(
    data.frame(chr = "chr3", start = 52197659, end = 52198659,
               name = "ALAS1_custom"),
    bed_file, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE
)
regions_from_bed <- prepare_regions(bed_file)
regions_from_bed
stopifnot(identical(start(regions), start(regions_from_bed)),
          identical(end(regions), end(regions_from_bed)))
```

For tables, declare `coordinate_system = "bed"` or `"one_based"` explicitly.
For gene-based selection, provide `annotation`, `genes` and `flank_bp`:

```{r annotation-regions}
# Synthetic plant annotation included to demonstrate GFF3 input.
plant_annotation <- system.file("extdata", "plant", "annotation.gff3",
    package = "selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")
plant_promoters <- prepare_regions(
    annotation = plant_annotation, genes = "AT5G00010", flank_bp = 1000
)
plant_promoters
```

Annotations must contain transcript/mRNA records with gene relationships.
Ordinary promoter selection does not require canonical tags. A flank of 1,000
selects one-based `[TSS - 1000, TSS + 999]`. The plant annotation above is a
separate illustration; continue using `regions` with the LCL sample sheet.

### `extract_canonical_tss()` — select canonical TSSs {#extract-canonical-tss}

Use this optional function when you specifically want canonical transcripts.
Specify the attribute and value used by your annotation; the defaults look
for GENCODE's `tag = Ensembl_canonical`. Missing or ambiguous canonical
selections raise an error.

```{r extract-canonical-tss}
canonical_tss <- extract_canonical_tss(
    annotation = plant_annotation,
    genes = "AT5G00010",
    attribute = "canonical", value = "true", flank_bp = 0
)
canonical_tss
```

`flank_bp = 0` returns the single TSS base. A positive flank returns a region
around it, ready for validation and analysis against matching tracks.

## Validate and analyze: tutorials

### `validate_inputs()` — check the inputs {#validate-inputs}

Check track paths, adjacent indexes, declared column counts and m6A contig
availability before analyzing. Success returns `TRUE` invisibly; an invalid
input raises an error describing the problem.

```{r validate-inputs}
valid <- validate_inputs(samples, regions)
valid
```

An optional track may have no calls on the selected contig. A supplied path to
a missing file is an error. All files and coordinates must use the same genome
assembly; validation cannot determine the biological assembly from names alone.

### `analyze_loci()` — collect calls and cluster reads {#analyze-loci}

Start without clustering. Here, `tf_length_ranges = NULL` retains all positive
TF lengths after the applicable score filter:

```{r analyze-unclustered}
unclustered <- analyze_loci(
    samples, regions, clustering = FALSE,
    nuc_min = 130, nuc_max = 160,
    min_tf_score = 50, tf_length_ranges = NULL,
    smoothing_bp = 10
)
x <- unclustered[["ALAS1_custom"]]
x
dim(assay(x, "m6a"))
```

The result is a named list of locus experiments. Each sparse assay has genomic
positions in rows and reads in columns. `colData(x)` contains read metadata and
per-read footprint ranges. Only reads whose longest overlapping alignment
spans the complete locus are retained, including reads with zero m6A calls.

For custom TF length filters, pass `list(c(30, 39), c(80, 120))` for inclusive
30–39 and 80–120 bp classes, or `list(c(35, 35))` for exactly 35 bp. Ranges must
have positive integer bounds and must not overlap. Omitting the argument
preserves the default 10–29, 40–59 and 60–79 bp classes. Both TF formats use the
same length filtering; only FiberHMM BED15 uses `min_tf_score`.

Run the same locus with clustering enabled:

```{r analyze-clustered}
clustered <- analyze_loci(
    samples, regions, clustering = TRUE,
    window_size = 50, k_neighbors = 5, resolution = 0.5, seed = 1,
    nuc_min = 130, nuc_max = 160,
    min_tf_score = 50, tf_length_ranges = NULL,
    smoothing_bp = 10
)
xc <- clustered[["ALAS1_custom"]]
S4Vectors::metadata(xc)$clustering_status
stopifnot(identical(S4Vectors::metadata(xc)$clustering_status, "complete"))
table(sample = colData(xc)$sample_label, cluster = colData(xc)$cluster)
```

`window_size` sets clustering bins in bp (`0` uses observed sites without
binning), `k_neighbors` sets the nearest-neighbor count, `resolution` controls
Leiden partition granularity, and `seed` controls randomness. Larger resolution
values generally favor more clusters. These illustrative settings are not
optimized biological parameters.

Clustering uses m6A patterns across the supplied samples at each locus. It needs
at least three reads and two occupied features; otherwise, metadata explain
why it was skipped. Exact Manhattan distances require memory quadratic in the
number of reads. Footprint filters do not affect the m6A fit. Binning does not
change the stored single-base assay, and `smoothing_bp` independently controls
profile smoothing.

## Summarize and visualize: tutorials

### `locus_profile()` — summarize m6A calls {#locus-profile}

Calculate a pooled profile from all retained reads, or separate profiles by
cluster. `frac` is the observed-call fraction and `smooth_frac` is its smoothed
value. Zero-call reads remain in the denominator.

```{r locus-profile}
pooled_profile <- locus_profile(x)
head(pooled_profile)

cluster_profiles <- locus_profile(xc, by_cluster = TRUE)
head(cluster_profiles)

# Clustering leaves the pooled profile unchanged.
stopifnot(identical(pooled_profile, locus_profile(xc)))
```

Sparse zeros indicate no observed m6A call, not a direct measurement of an
unmethylated adenine at every genomic base. Subsetting reads in an experiment
and calling `locus_profile()` recomputes the profile for those reads.

### `plot_locus()` — draw locus figures {#plot-locus}

Choose `"heatmap"`, `"profile"` or `"footprints"`. The heatmap shows reads on the
y-axis and positions on the x-axis. The footprint composition stacks the m6A
profile, m6A reads and supplied footprint tracks.

```{r unclustered-heatmap, fig.height=7}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(x, "heatmap"))
```

```{r unclustered-profile}
plot_locus(x, "profile")
```

```{r unclustered-footprints, fig.height=10}
plot_locus(x, "footprints")
```

Use `clustered = TRUE` to order reads by existing assignments and display
per-cluster profiles. This does not rerun clustering.

```{r clustered-heatmap, fig.height=7}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(xc, "heatmap", clustered = TRUE))
```

```{r clustered-profile}
plot_locus(xc, "profile", clustered = TRUE)
```

```{r clustered-footprints, fig.height=10}
plot_locus(xc, "footprints", clustered = TRUE)
```

Custom TF ranges receive labels and colors automatically. If supplied
nucleosome or TF tracks contain no retained calls, analysis emits
`no footprints called in the selected region` and continues. Check read IDs,
length bounds and score thresholds when calls were expected.

### `cluster_colors()` — reuse cluster colors {#cluster-colors}

Retrieve the plotting palette for cluster labels or factor levels. Use it to
keep your own figures consistent with the locus plots.

```{r cluster-colors}
palette <- cluster_colors(colData(xc)$cluster)
palette

# Named colors can also be requested directly.
cluster_colors(c("cluster1", "cluster2", "cluster3"))
```

Numeric cluster IDs retain their colors when a cluster is absent from a subset.
Keep complete factor levels for palettes containing more than 25 clusters.

## Export results: tutorial

### `write_locus_results()` — save the analysis {#write-locus-results}

Pass a single locus experiment or the complete results list, and choose a new
or empty output directory. This example exports all loci from the clustered
run, including both unclustered and clustered views:

```{r write-locus-results}
output_dir <- tempfile("fiberseq-reference-results-")
write_locus_results(clustered, output_dir)
list.files(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Each locus directory includes `locus.rds`, `m6a_matrix.rds`, read/QC/region TSVs,
and PDF figures. Successful clustering adds assignments and graph edges.
Replace `tempfile()` with a persistent folder to keep the results.

```{r reload-results}
restored <- readRDS(file.path(output_dir, "ALAS1_custom", "locus.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(assay(restored), assay(xc)),
          identical(colData(restored), colData(xc)))
```

Reload `locus.rds` to retain the full experiment, including footprints and run
parameters. The matrix-only RDS does not contain that additional information.
